blocks.heading: The shop steward’s work
blocks.text: A shop steward can gather members’ concerns, explain union information, represent workers in discussions, help members use agreed grievance arrangements and keep them informed about negotiations. The steward should check facts and communicate the members’ position accurately. Representation is different from authority to manage the enterprise or decide every issue unilaterally. A credible steward can help clarify misunderstanding before a disagreement grows, while recognising when support from wider union officials is needed. Effective links require listening to members as well as speaking to management.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Nura Goods’ workers receive inconsistent explanations of a changed rota. Their steward gathers the questions and meets management. A verified shared list can focus discussion and reduce rumours. Reporting the response back to members closes the communication loop rather than leaving workers uncertain about what was agreed.
